A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Mirror Descent Under Generalized Smoothness. Their main text, figures, table, equations, and Appendices A–K are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v3 reports original nanoGPT training-trajectory measurements and numerical gradient/Hessian experiments on synthetic functions in Section 2.3 and Appendices B and C.3.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and reports additional GPT-2, WMT’16 Transformer, and CIFAR-10 CNN measurements, including full-batch CNN experiments.

M1.justification: The mirror descent, accelerated, optimistic, mirror-prox, stochastic, and composite update procedures and step-size rules are retained, including Appendix J. Additional implementation explanations and learning-rate guidance do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: v3 evaluates nanoGPT on FineWeb and synthetic functions. v4 retains this coverage and adds WMT’16 experiments with a six-layer Transformer and CIFAR-10 multiclass image classification, substantially broadening the represented data and tasks.

E2.justification: No competing optimizer is added to or removed from an empirical comparison. The synthetic Euclidean/non-Euclidean comparison and measured-versus-affine curvature fits are retained. AdamW appears in practical guidance, not as a newly evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Beyond v3's nanoGPT-124M setup, v4 reports 355M and 770M GPT-2 configurations, introduces full-dataset gradients for a CNN control, and adds an ℓ1-curvature/ℓ∞-gradient diagnostic for WMT’16. These substantially expand evaluation settings; the retained synthetic sampling protocol is unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 2.3 and Figure 4 add a full-batch CNN analysis testing whether the curvature-gradient relationship persists without minibatch gradient noise. v3 has no equivalent control. The existing synthetic dimension-sensitivity analysis in Appendix C.3 is retained.

E5.justification: Relative-MSE fit diagnostics already appear in v3. Neither version reports experimental repeat counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The theoretical high-probability guarantees are also unchanged.

E6.justification: The single main nanoGPT plot is replaced by size-specific GPT-2 results and a Transformer plot; CNN results and a fifth nanoGPT block are added. Newly reported relative MSE values include 0.0005 for GPT-2-small and 0.0091 for block 4. These are curvature-fit results, not same-setting predictive performance gains. The synthetic slope fit remains 1.87 n^(-0.43).

T1.justification: Proposition 2.8 now treats a quartic function, with a new proof and exact-link comparison in Appendix C.1; the earlier logistic examples remain in C.1.1–C.1.2. New Appendix C.4 derives block-diagonal smoothness as a special case. The central smoothness definitions and optimization convergence theorems are retained.

C1.justification: The introduction explicitly adds empirical validation across LLMs and CNNs to the claimed contributions. The principal claims about non-Euclidean generalized smoothness and matching classical convergence rates remain unchanged in the abstract and conclusion.

C2.justification: v4 adds a Hessian-heterogeneity rationale for testing CNNs, explains the distinction between convenient affine links and tighter exact links, and states that full-batch validation is restricted to CNNs because it is computationally infeasible for LLMs. Appendix J.3 also removes the earlier mutual non-implication statement about generalized heavy-tailed noise conditions.

D1.justification: Appendix B explicitly identifies nanoGPT as the GPT-2 implementation and adds guidance on choosing learning rates using a previously recorded AdamW trajectory. The existing code-access information, PyTorch/DDP implementation, and eight 24GB NVIDIA 4090 GPUs are retained.

R1.justification: New Appendix C.4 positions the framework relative to block-diagonal smoothness and Hessian heterogeneity, citing An et al. (2025) and Zhang et al. (2024c). Additional citations address the new experiments and heavy-tailed optimization. The principal comparisons with Li et al. and relative smoothness remain intact.

P1.justification: v4 adds an introduction contribution list, consolidates notation in Section 2, rewrites the examples and empirical subsection, and inserts Appendix C.4. Affiliations, publication information, acknowledgements, and some grammar are updated. The main section order and most exposition remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The single-panel main Figure 1 becomes a four-panel display. v4 adds two six-panel CNN figures and expands the appendix transformer-block figure from four to five panels. The synthetic figures are retained as Figures 5–6, and Table 1 remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: Compared with v3's nanoGPT-centered validation, v4 strengthens evidence for practical applicability across model families and adds a full-batch check addressing gradient-noise confounding. The quartic and block-diagonal derivations also clarify the framework's coverage. The central theoretical results remain unchanged, and the new experimental settings are only briefly documented, making the overall gain useful but limited.
